name: JOHNSON & JOHNSON HEALTH CARE SYSTEMS INC.
agency: Department of Health and Human Services
brief_text:
Four detectors flagged Johnson & Johnson Health Care Systems Inc. for statistical anomalies. Benford's Law analysis of leading digits in award amounts showed a severe departure from expected frequency patterns, with digit 3 appearing far more often than natural. Modification growth on a single parent contract expanded at 737 times its initial value, vastly outpacing peers in the medical instrument sector. The entity also registered as a multivariate outlier across multiple dimensions including award concentration and competition patterns. Finally, sole-source awards comprised 98 percent of its portfolio, compared to a median of 1.4 percent among comparable firms.

The Benford test yielded a Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic of 0.228 with p-value near zero across 1,073 transactions. The worst modification contract grew at a ratio of 737.6 versus a peer average of 55.5, producing a z-score of 5.1. The isolation forest score reached 0.87 on a 0-to-1 scale. Sole-source awards totaled 1,052 of 1,073 awards, a 98 percent concentration; peers in NAICS 423450 averaged 1.4 percent with standard deviation of 0.29, yielding a z-score of 3.3.

These statistical signals warrant scrutiny but do not prove fraud. Johnson & Johnson's scale—61.4 million lifetime obligated value across 1,074 awards—and its position as an established medical device manufacturer may explain some patterns. However, the extreme sole-source concentration and Benford deviation are unusual even for large incumbents and merit investigation into contract justifications and pricing practices.
